summary: Dorothy Maskell worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. Succeeding William Stede, she served as Reader of Pāli at SOAS University of London from 1949 to 1956.

Douglas Allen is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Yale, Banaras Hindu University, and Vanderbilt. He taught at Southern Illinois University and Central Connecticut State before a long career at the University of Maine from 1974.

Douglas Barrett was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied classics at Oxford and attended SOAS. He served at the British Museum from 1947, working as Curator from 1969 to 1977, and was elected a British Academy Fellow in 1976.

Douglas Craven Phillott worked in linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology after attending Felsted School and the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst. He was a Fellow of The Asiatic Society and became Lecturer in Urdu and Hindustani at Gonville and Caius College in 1912.

Douglas Gildow specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, completing a PhD at Princeton under Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou. He held posts at City College of New York and Florida State before becoming Assistant Professor at CUHK in 2018.
Douglas J. Penick is an author in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Princeton University from around 1962 to 1966 and studied under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1971.

Douglas L. Berger works in philosophy, Sinology, and Indology. His appointments include Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (attested 2007-2014) and Professor and Centre Director at Leiden University (attested 2026).

Douglas Ober works in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Harjot Oberoi (attested 2016).

Douglas Osto, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Grinnell, Harvard, the University of Washington, and earned his PhD at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. He joined Massey University in 2005, becoming Senior Lecturer around 2007.

Douglas Q. Adams is a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago from around 1967 to 1972 and held a post at the University of Idaho around 1972.

Douglas S. Duckworth works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at James Madison and the University of Virginia (PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins) and held teaching posts at Rangjung Yeshe Institute and East Tennessee State University.
Dragana Majhen studied religious studies and Buddhist studies at the University of Manitoba, earning a master's degree under thesis advisor Albert Welter (attested 2010).

Dragomir Dimitrov works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, completing his MA and PhD under Michael Hahn at the University of Marburg. He held posts at Marburg, the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Dramdul works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as Director of the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2004-2012) and editor-in-chief of Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (attested 2015).
Drodul Dorji Tenzin studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Drodul Pawo Dorje studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Ayu Khandro, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Drolkar Chungchung studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Drolma studied Tibetology at the University of Oslo, completing an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Drubwang Shakya Shri studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

id: P:Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé
summary: Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.
